correctness.rationale: Simultaneous Boolean spectral projections give an inverse pair of constructions between ordered commuting idempotents and labeled complete orthogonal families, including zero projectors and characteristic two. For the standard family d_alpha formed from the e_i, any family f_alpha with the same quotient has u=sum f_alpha d_alpha in 1+J and u d_alpha=f_alpha u. Distinct quotient colorings cannot be related by any unit, as A/J is commutative. Independently, write J=J_diag plus J_cross by same-color and cross-color Peirce blocks. The stabilizer in 1+J is exactly 1+J_diag, since commuting with all d_alpha is the same as being block diagonal. Each right coset has a unique representative 1+x with x in J_cross: right multiply any unit of 1+J by the inverse of its block diagonal part; off-block stays off-block and the resulting diagonal is 1, proving both existence and uniqueness. Thus the exact orbit index is q^(dim J_cross)=q^d(c) and also counts the full-unit orbit. The Q^n colorings cover the entire tuple locus without coordinate permutations. Expanding X+(1-X)delta on each individual edge counts Q^k(F) colorings per chosen edge subset, including parallel edges and isolated vertices. In the two-cycle quotients, each direction has exactly s odd paths strictly below either cutoff, so d(c) is 0 or 2s as claimed. The radical consists of positive-length paths; the longest surviving path certifies each distinct nilpotency index. Equal cardinality multisets do not imply equal stabilizers or unit groups. The supplied small-case enumeration was inspected, not executed, and is not needed for the all-parameter proof.

value.rationale: The multiset for all arities is a natural refinement of a count of Boolean idempotent decompositions. The Peirce law explains which data survive and which disappear, even beyond radical-square-zero algebras. The connected two-vertex examples have nontrivial off-diagonal cut weights and prove that this complete size-only invariant cannot detect different and arbitrarily large Loewy lengths; this structural limitation is stronger than a single numerical coincidence or the prior incidence enumeration.
